Theme

Computing & programming

variable noun

in programming or mathematics

also variables, declare a variable, constant

* our formation

* (our own formation) variābilis, variābilis f.

noun (sc. quantitās), third declension

a variable

Our use, shortened from quantitās variābilis, the variable quantity of eighteenth-century mathematics; a constant is quantitās cōnstāns. The adjective variābilis is post-classical (Apul.).

Other words

  • quantitās variābilis — a variable quantity

    also used · modern · Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (1748), 1.2 (not checked against the text)

    The full term, as mathematicians wrote it.

See also variable, programming, code, value.

SourcesLewis & Short: variabilis · Lewis & Short: quantitas

Leonhard Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (Lausanne, 1748), vol. 1, ch. 1, §2 (quantitās variābilis); the reference is given from memory and has not been checked against the text. Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for a variable.
